observations:
Torah LM2/50 does not contain three or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language. The text is a short, self-contained practical instruction about controlling wandering thought. Its structure is entirely that of an eitza (cause-and-effect / practical guidance) teaching:

  Thought wanders to foreign matters (cause) → You can forcibly redirect it (action) → It returns to the straight path (effect).

The central concepts mentioned are: מַחֲשָׁבָה (thought), דֶּרֶךְ הַיָּשָׁר (the straight path), דְּבָרִים זָרִים (alien matters), and the mashal pair סוּס / אַפְסָר (horse / halter). None of these are equated with each other using bechina language. The mashal is introduced with 'כְּמוֹ סוּס' (like a horse) — the language of comparison, not the language of identity ('הוּא בְּחִינַת' or 'נִקְרָא'). A mashal that says 'the mind is LIKE a horse' does not create a bechina relationship; it is an illustrative analogy operating within the eitza argument.

Because the source text provides no bechina language connecting independent conceptual domains, and the dataset contains zero bechina edges for this Torah, no new packages can be proposed.
